newsitem.title: JAPAN: High Japan product stocks force run-cuts, exports.
newsitem.headline: High Japan product stocks force run-cuts, exports.

text.p: High product inventories, which have loomed as a bearish factor in Japan refinery economics since March, look to be hitting the sector this week, with one refiner resorting to a marginal cut in throughputs, and another exporting surplus supplies to China and the United States.
Cosmo Oil Co Ltd said on Monday it had reduced runs by some one to two percent as a result of bulging inventories and lacklustre customer demand in the months of April and May.
"The cuts reflect a natural easing because of the high level of product inventories we are currently experiencing in Japan," a Cosmo Oil spokesman said.

A trader with Showa Shell Sekiyu KK said the refiner had already begun exports of middle distillates to China, as well as gasoline blending component to the United States, in order to relieve the overhang.
"We are not considering refinery run cuts at this stage, although our refinery margins are not so good," the trader said.
"But we have been exporting product to both China and the U.S., and will look to increase those volumes," he added.

Asian crude oil markets have been speculating for the last few days that Japanese refiners would resort to cutting refinery runs in the coming weeks in light of high product stocks, as well as weather forecasts predicting cooler-than-normal summer temperatures across much of Japan.
Summer is normally a period of high demand for Japanese refiners, as Japan's blistering summers maximise air-conditioning usage and lead to an increase in fuel oil burning by power utilities.
Since late 1996, unseasonably mild winter temperatures have seen Japan's domestic stocks of refined products swell to levels some 20 percent higher than year-ago levels.
